item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded: I'm too late to vote against now but I felt like that addition was just shoehorned in so there would be further pages to visit. 3530 doesn't even use D classes, does it? I mean WikiWalks sounds like a program centered AROUND directing me to more pages to read, which is a sensible action for the WEBSITE to take, but I'm not sure if it's a sensible action for the in-universe Foundation to take. Maybe I'm wrong about what that program does though, idk. Those D-class aren't any better than others for feeding purposes, except maybe those SCPs all seem to tell the difference between paedophiles and non, but containment procedures never really provide for continuous use of D classes in those three, and paedophiles aren't specifically required by the house for sustenance (unless this is an unusually implicit method of saying it does in a containment procedures write-up where realizing information clearly can save lives). There's no NEED to always take any D classes tested in occasional tests on those three and make them get eaten by the house because the tests on those three are probably so infrequent that creating separate procedure for dealing with a not-special group is logistically unhelpful. They don't have so many D classes from the three that they need a special place to get rid of them; I doubt they ever become unable to handle an amount, and some tales describe SHORTAGES. They should just treat them like normal D classes because nothing is changed about them, and the Foundation shouldn't try to create symbolic justice going out of their way to feed paedophiles to that thing.

The main description seems pretty self-contained but the containment procedures leave room for stuff to be added. Therefore I propose the following edit:

Once monthly, one Class-D with a history of child abuse is to be released into the structure housing SCP-789. D-Class previously scheduled tested with SCP-204, SCP-2672, and SCP-3530 have been used historically for this purpose.

item.title: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded: Just as a note, version 21 of this article made an edit which technically falls outside of what is allowed by general users on pages by other authors. The capitalization of subdesignations in SCP articles is up to the author, and as such shouldn't be changed to be one way or the other. In this case, the author gave retroactive approval, so the edit was not reverted, but the point still stands.

What would really make it shine is some unexpected revelation once the prey shows up, I think, to subvert the subversion. Okay, so it lures the prey in, makes them at home, asks them to take a seat, something happens, they're crushed to a fine slurry - what else happens during that time? Do the consciousnesses of the child molesters continue on in some form? What happens if the building is moved? What happens when a Class-D is introduced into the house without the inverted grooming happening (as is suggested by the severing of the telephone and internet lines)? What happens when containment fails, and someone is drawn to the house without having been called first?

I agree with everything here, except it's not a hotel, it's a house. I think that the root problem is that the idea feels too complete, and it's too small an idea for that to work. There's no element of mystery, and I don't think that one can be introduced through better writing.

On one hand, the idea is, I believe, executed perfectly. I don't think that this idea could be written much better, so, credit where it's due. On the other hand, the idea is bad. Well, it's not so much that the idea is bad as it is that the idea simply doesn't translate into the SCP format.
